sections.title: 1. Why Study Computer Engineering in Ireland?

items: Computer Engineering is the combination of computer hardware, electronics, embedded systems and software. A postgraduate degree can help graduates gain specialist skills for careers in technology, telecommunications, semiconductor systems, automation and intelligent devices.
Key benefits of studying in Ireland include:
- Advanced technical education: Learn computer architecture, embedded systems, digital design, electronic systems, and hardware-software integration.
Specialisation possibilities: Choose modules related to robotics, signal processing, communications, Internet of Things (IoT) or intelligent systems, depending on the program.
Exposure to the tech industry: Ireland has a large tech industry with opportunities in multinationals, engineering firms and research organizations.
Practical projects: Many programs include laboratory work, technical assignments and a master’s project.
Career flexibility: Graduates can work in hardware engineering, embedded software, systems engineering, electronics and other technical fields.
Further research: A masters could lay the groundwork for doctorate research or specialized engineering development.
Students can explore these opportunities and learn about the requirements of pursuing education abroad with Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance.

sections.title: 4. Eligibility of PG in Computer Engineering in Ireland

items: For most postgraduate engineering courses you will need a relevant bachelor’s degree and an appropriate academic record.
Some common requirements are:
An undergraduate degree recognized as a BE, BTech or equivalent.
A degree in Computer Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering or any other accepted related field.
Minimum marks or required academic classification.
Relevant prior work in mathematics, electronics, digital systems or computer engineering.
English language skills, if necessary.
Indian students eligibility
Indian applicants are typically evaluated on the basis of bachelor’s degree, recognition of university, CGPA or percentage, duration of the course, and subject content.
A BE or BTech in Computer Engineering, Electronics and Communication Engineering, Electrical Engineering or related discipline may be suitable for the program.

sections.title: 5. Admission Requirements for PG Computer Engineering in Ireland

items: Universities will be looking at both academic suitability and supporting documents
Academic accomplishments
You may be required to supply:
Bachelor’s degree certificate or provisional certificate
Official transcript for each year/semester.
A copy of the grading scale or the CGPA conversion, if needed.
Information of relevant modules or technical projects.
Proof of work experience, if applicable
Requirements in English Language
International students may be required to take the IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic or an approved test.

For example, the published requirements for the UCD Electronic and Computer Engineering master's are IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 or accepted equivalent. Other universities and programs may have different limits.
Additional requirements
You may also have to: Depending on the institution for
Statement of purpose.
References of academic or professional nature.
Résumé or curriculum vitae.
Details about research or engineering projects
Pay the application fee.
Other documents necessary for qualification evaluation.

items: 8\. Computer Engineering Accreditation & Recognition in Ireland
If you want to pursue a professional engineering career, it is important to check accreditation.

In Ireland, Engineers Ireland accredits qualifying engineering programs to professional education standards. However, accreditation is programme-specific, and not all master’s programs are accredited separately.
Before you sign up, make sure:
Whether the particular program and award are recognized.
The years of graduation that the accreditation covers.
If the program satisfies the academic requirements for your intended professional engineering pathway.
Whether your bachelor’s degree also needs to satisfy certain academic requirements.
Other requirements from your future employer or country of destination.
A postgraduate qualification will enhance your technical skills, but it will not necessarily lead to professional registration or recognition in any country

faqs.q: 1\. What are the universities offering postgraduate Computer Engineering courses in Ireland?
faqs.a: Options include DCU's MEng in Electronic and Computer Engineering, UCD's Master's in Electronic and Computer Engineering, the University of Galway's ME in Electronic and Computer Engineering, and Trinity College Dublin's MSc in Electronic Information Engineering.

faqs.q: 2\. How long does a postgraduate Computer Engineering course last?
faqs.a: Many full-time taught master’s in engineering programmes take one year. Other programs and research degrees might be longer. Please check the length of your chosen program.

faqs.q: 3\. Can a B.Tech student of computer science or IT apply?
faqs.a: It is possible, but entry is subject to the course. Engineering courses with a hardware focus may require you to have studied electronics, circuits, signals or other engineering subjects previously. Check the programme’s acceptable degree backgrounds before you apply.

faqs.q: 4\. What is the cost of PG Computer Engineering in Ireland?
faqs.a: 2026/27 Courses : Non-EU tuition fees for the listed courses range from €25,000 at DCU to €29,500 at UCD. Living expenses are additional and fees may vary by intake.
